derived.prompt: Wolves are vossel-tied to elk, and elk are vossel-tied to aspen trees. Does it follow that wolves are vossel-tied to aspen trees?
bridge: Wolves are vossel-tied to elk, and elk are vossel-tied to aspen trees.
chain: Wolves are vossel-tied to elk. (given in prompt)
Elk are vossel-tied to aspen trees. (given in prompt)
So wolves are vossel-tied to aspen trees: yes, it follows.

derived.prompt: Sea otters are vossel-tied to sea urchins, and sea urchins are vossel-tied to kelp. Given only these two facts, could sea otters fail to be vossel-tied to kelp?
bridge: Sea otters are vossel-tied to sea urchins, and sea urchins are vossel-tied to kelp.
chain: Sea otters are vossel-tied to sea urchins. (given in prompt)
Sea urchins are vossel-tied to kelp. (given in prompt)
So sea otters are vossel-tied to kelp: no, they could not fail to be.

'Is vossel-tied to' is transitive..why: "Vossel-tied" is a made-up relation (catalogued as vossel_tied_to, fictional, no property tags): it is not a term anyone uses, its words carry no built-in sense of chaining, so a model has no default reading of it as transitive. The instances are real food-chain organisms that could be tied by it without a record already knowing.

Sea otters are mammals..why: The first sentence of the sea otter article.

sources.quote: The sea otter is a marine mammal native to the coasts of the northern and eastern North Pacific Ocean.

sources.query: the sea otter is a marine mammal

Elk are reptiles..why: Deliberately false so the disjunction turns on the inserted property: the elk is a large deer.

sources.quote: The elk or wapiti is the second largest species within the deer family, Cervidae, and one of the largest terrestrial mammals in its native range of North America and Central and East Asia.

notes: RBox expansion paired with biology-replace-0009 ('is part of' loses transitivity): gives a made-up relation (vossel_tied_to, transitive) the property the revision changes, applied to real instances in the prompt. Instances are food-chain triples (wolves, elk, aspen; sea otters, sea urchins, kelp); the direct, first instance and cross-lingual answers are yes, the second instance ('could fail') is no. The coined terms stay untranslated in the Chinese and Spanish prompts. hops counts the prompt facts as one bridge. Unrelated near and far ask other properties of real relations that the edit must not change. Locality references are the logical answers; scoring uses each model's own pre-edit answer. Known weakness: these are textbook trophic cascades, so a model may answer yes from real ecology without the edit.
